items.item: Reading views share the specified text hierarchy, control identities, and sentence-anchor grammar through overlays, appearance changes, reflow, and selected continuation records.
Day, Night, large-text, and wide variants preserve their required content and position meanings; Night uses #18252B and may use a lighter related action accent for contrast.
Playback and handover views follow the specified control language and remain visually coherent with Reader while distinguishing preview, playing, paused, speed, timer, and offline states.
Media offsets, nominal chapter durations, and timer settings remain distinct concepts, with the prescribed defaults and state-specific values.
Catalog, download, empty, and choice screens share the specification's component geometry, visual hierarchy, status vocabulary, navigation language, and accent treatment.
File availability, download progress, device provenance, and saved positions remain visibly distinct, and state colours always have words or symbols.

carryThrough.none: The specification is an image role, and the only document role is the downstream presentation, from which no later file must repeat written facts.

requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect the complete SHA-bound original film and confirm the stated length and final stage. The video slot is scored on delivery only; duration is not read automatically, because a correct segmented delivery and a provider generation cap are both indistinguishable from a short film to a property reader. This is a complete-original manual check, not a scored output or human acceptance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Assess the internal logical screen envelope and proportional safe-area bands, independently of export pixel dimensions. Standard screens follow the 390:844 envelope with 47/34 logical-unit top/bottom insets; reader-wide follows 430:932 with 59/34 insets. Required copy and complete controls remain inside the safe region. Each image depicts one flat screen, with any named overlay on its actual underlying screen; its complete frame is proportionally centred within the delivery canvas. Clipping, stretching, or controls intruding into protected bands fails.

Evaluate foreground/background contrast for visible body text against 4.5:1 and for large text and meaningful icons against 3:1. Every status communicated through colour also has readable wording or a recognizable symbol. Supporting colours may vary, but low-contrast content or a status distinguishable only by colour fails.

Both screens identify the two distinct supplied books with their exact titles and attribute both to PAGEWIND Studio. PAGEWIND is visibly printed as the product name. Book records must not be duplicated, interchanged, or omitted; any displayed chapter counts, narration totals, and chapter titles agree with the supplied records. Layout and explanatory wording may vary.

Library and Downloads display the three named main destinations in the prescribed reading order. Other main-area navigation, when present, preserves that order. Reader, Player, settings overlays, mode-switch screens, and continuation choices expose an identifiable return action. Icons may accompany labels, and return controls may use conventional symbols; missing destinations, reordered main navigation, or a missing required return action fails.

Every depicted cover for The Small Lantern visibly uses lantern-cover-art.png and remains associated with the correct title. Proportional scaling within the cover treatment is acceptable; replacing it with newly invented lantern art or assigning it to The Empty Bench fails. Screens with no cover depiction do not need an added cover.

Read each screen against its named row in 05-state-snapshots.md, distinguishing connection, device, sentence anchor, chapter-relative offset, playback, local file availability, and save/sync status where relevant. Core Library shows paused L1 at 00:37 and the L2 download in progress; the four core snapshots use the 08:20 synced record. Downloads distinguishes saved L1/L2 text, ready L1 audio, incomplete L2 audio, and The Empty Bench text not downloaded with narration not offered. Other states must preserve their supplied records. Equivalent chapter-and-sentence wording is allowed, and irrelevant record fields need not be printed; contradictory state data or treating a received record as already applied fails.

The specification is the stated source for subsequent screen decisions. Its page table covers all 21 named screens with entries, relevant data, and named states; its component table connects default, pressed, disabled, and error states to concrete control values. It records brand and Night colours, contrast ratios meeting the required thresholds, both logical safe-area envelopes, navigation order, control options, and sentence-location grammar. Position rules include start-inclusive/end-exclusive intervals, 00:37 mapping to L1-S03, 00:45 mapping to L1-S04, unchanged media offsets after speed changes, anchor preservation through reflow, and an explicit next-chapter action at chapter end. Download and continuation rules explain completeness before offline playback, local retention, explicit record choice, cancellation, and the received-record application outcome. Missing state coverage, unspecified values, or contradictory rules fails.

The standard and wide Reader use the specified default control identities and state treatments. Offline-unavailable visibly uses the specified disabled Listen state with a readable error explanation. Reflow may move content, but controls remain complete and their state meanings stay consistent across envelopes. An enabled-looking blocked action or a state conveyed only by colour fails; pressed feedback is assessed in the film check.

All six views retain chapter 1 sentence 3 and the original L1 wording from 04-chapter-text-and-timeline.md. The complete six-sentence chapter remains available in the reading flow; line wrapping, scrolling, and pagination may change without changing its content or anchor. Reader defaults to 18/Day with Listen; reader-settings offers 18, 22, 26 and Day/Night with 18/Day selected; reader-night uses 18/Night and background #18252B; reader-large uses 26/Day; reader-wide uses 18/Day with genuine reflow. Losing the anchor, paraphrasing text, scaling the entire standard screen instead of reflowing, or wrong appearance values fails.

Core Player plays L1 at 00:37 of nominal 01:30 with Read, speed 1.0x, and timer Off, with 1.5x available. The timer overlay selects 15 minutes from the three supplied choices at the same offset. Player-speed plays at 1.5x while retaining 00:37/01:30 and timer Off. Timer-expired shows playback paused at 00:37 with Resume available. Timer-expired is a separate fixed snapshot; do not calculate a later playback offset from the timer selection. Altered nominal duration, moved media position, or an incorrect playing/paused state fails.

The delivered states form a coherent transition: Reader is at L1-S03; switch-to-audio labels 00:30 as the proposed sentence start, retains the stored 00:37 offset, and requires Confirm; Player shows the later playing state at 00:37; switch-to-text shows playback paused at 00:37 with L1-S03 open. Listen, Confirm, and Read identify their respective actions. Equivalent sentence-location wording is acceptable. Applying the preview before confirmation, confusing proposed and stored positions, or returning to another sentence fails.

Review the complete 12-second film against the four delivered source designs. It shows Reader at L1-S03, Listen leading to the 00:30 preview while stored 00:37 is retained, a visible Confirm press with pressed feedback, playback beginning only after confirmation at 00:30, progress to 00:37, and Read returning to L1-S03 with playback paused. The actual delivered interfaces must be visibly reused. Silence is allowed. Missing or reordered steps, playback before confirmation, wrong positions, or substituted interface designs fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The online Downloads state and both incomplete offline states retain L2 audio at 6 of 10 MB/60%; offline states make the paused transfer and listening block clear. Offline-unavailable distinguishes proposed 00:15 from saved L2-S02/00:22 and offers Open saved text. Resume-local retains that record with local save 08:40 and sync pending. Download-paused provides a reconnection/resume route. Download-complete is a later offline snapshot with 10 of 10 MB/100% available after successful online completion; offline-player uses that complete file to play L2 at 00:22, 1.0x, timer Off, with local save and sync pending. Progress indicators may vary visually, but equating file percentage with playback or enabling partial-file offline listening fails.

Sync-choice identifies Phone A's local L2-S02/00:22 save at 08:40 and Tablet B's received L2-S04/00:50 record synced at 08:35, dated 24 August 2027. Each has an explicit selection action; cancellation retains Phone A's position. Resume-remote shows the selected Tablet B position applied on Phone A, paused at L2 00:50 with text anchor L2-S04 and confirmed sync at 08:41. Equivalent date formatting is acceptable. Applying a record before choice, confusing source device with current device, or retaining the earlier sync time as the result fails.

The empty Library identifies offline Phone C, shows no local books, downloads, or saved progress, and provides a route to go online and add a book. It may acknowledge the existing two-book catalog without representing those books as already added or locally available. Showing Phone A's collection or progress on this device fails.

The presentation visibly reuses the delivered specification and every one of the 21 screen designs. It includes the handover sequence and paired views of related states, including incomplete versus complete offline availability and continuation choice versus applied result. Scaling and page arrangement may vary; substituted designs, mere textual references, or any omitted source fails.

The document has at least 12 pages and an index identifying all 21 delivered screen sources. It preserves the specification's #1F4E5F accent, main-navigation order, and sentence-anchor grammar. Its handover account distinguishes preview 00:30 from stored 00:37 until confirmation and shows playback followed by the paused Read return to L1-S03. Paired comparisons explain 6-of-10-MB/60% blocked offline audio versus 10-of-10-MB/100% readiness and subsequent L2 playback at 00:22; they distinguish the blocked 00:15 proposal from the saved L2-S02/00:22 record. The continuation comparison reproduces both dated records, explicit choice and cancellation, and the applied Tablet B L2-S04/00:50 result synced at 08:41. Page organization may vary; missing comparisons, insufficient pages, an incomplete index, or conflicting records fails.

Reading views share the specified text hierarchy, control identities, and sentence-anchor grammar through overlays, appearance changes, reflow, and selected continuation records. Day, Night, large-text, and wide variants preserve their required content and position meanings; Night uses #18252B and may use a lighter related action accent for contrast.

Playback and handover views follow the specified control language and remain visually coherent with Reader while distinguishing preview, playing, paused, speed, timer, and offline states. Media offsets, nominal chapter durations, and timer settings remain distinct concepts, with the prescribed defaults and state-specific values.

Catalog, download, empty, and choice screens share the specification's component geometry, visual hierarchy, status vocabulary, navigation language, and accent treatment. File availability, download progress, device provenance, and saved positions remain visibly distinct, and state colours always have words or symbols.
